correctness.rationale: Any nontrivial tensor factor of a split local algebra is again split local, and the radical of B⊗C is J(B)⊗C+B⊗J(C); quotienting by its square gives e(B⊗C)=e(B)+e(C). Since e(A)=2 and every nontrivial split local factor has e≥1, a nontrivial decomposition has e(B)=e(C)=1. For split local R with e=1, nilpotent J and a generator x of J/J² ensure every nonzero layer J^j/J^{j+1} is generated by x^j and has dimension exactly one, hence R≅k[t]/(t^m). Tensoring two such algebras gives the rectangular quotient; uniqueness of unordered irreducible factors follows from Sakurai Theorem A, with no characteristic restriction. Independent algebraic boundary checks: e=2 but k[x,y]/(x,y)² has dimension 3 so cannot be a tensor product of factors each dimension at least 2, whereas k[u,v]/(u²,v³) has Hilbert series 1+2t+2t²+t³. No numerical tests are offered as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The cotangent dimension two case is the first nontrivial embedding dimension; giving a full tensor-decomposability recognition theorem and unique explicit factor types is a natural complete classification beyond abstract uniqueness. It includes noncommutative associative local algebras and arbitrary field characteristic. The mathematical value is an exact structural boundary, not novelty of cotangent additivity alone.

final_claim: Every finite-dimensional associative unital split local k-algebra with dim_k J/J²=2 admits a nontrivial tensor decomposition over k iff it is a rectangular truncated polynomial algebra k[u,v]/(u^m,v^n) for integers m,n≥2; the unordered factor truncations are uniquely determined, and every noncommutative algebra in this class is tensor-indecomposable.
limitations: Split finite-dimensional associative unital local algebras, field tensor products and embedding dimension exactly two; no classification in higher dimensions or nonsplit cases.
Sakurai uniqueness is credited, not claimed as new, and no independent certification or Lean proof is inferred.
